sources.fullCitation: Tihoti-re et son ensemble tahitien, with vocal duo by Mlle Maéva and Tihoti; presented by E. Ventrillon. “O chant d’amour de Tahiti !”, from Les révoltés du Bounty, credited to B. Kaper, W. Jurmann and G. Rey, composers / “Ho’i-maï”, credited to G. Rey, composer and lyricist. [Paris]: [Industries Musicales et Electriques Pathé-Marconi], [DL 1940]. One 25 cm 78 rpm disc, Pathé PA 1234, matrices CPT 3351 and CPT 3352. Recording date given as 23 June 1937. Bibliothèque nationale de France, Catalogue général, FRBNF37963787, ARK ark:/12148/cb37963787p.
sources.title: O chant d’amour de Tahiti ! / Ho’i-maï — Pathé PA 1234
sources.creator: Bronisław Kaper, Walter Jurmann, Georges Rey
sources.repository: Bibliothèque nationale de France / Catalogue général
sources.researchNote: The BnF publication statement is [DL 1940]: this denotes legal deposit, not an independently established commercial issue date. The catalogue separately states “Enregistrement : 19370623”; the structured date follows that recording date, 23 June 1937. UNIMARC field 101 gives language code tah, Tahitian, for the disc; the French title alone does not establish the language of the sung text. The catalogue lists Rey as a composer alongside Kaper and Jurmann for “O chant d’amour de Tahiti !”; the 1935 copyright entry and 1936 French sheet-music catalogue name Kaper and Jurmann as composers. Rey’s contribution and the reason for the discrepancy remain unresolved. BnF separately credits him as composer and lyricist of the coupling “Ho’i-maï”. The two matrices are listed together without an explicit title-by-title assignment.

sources.fullCitation: Bibliothèque nationale de France. Notice de personne “Rey, Georges (1908–2011)”, FRBNF16974300, ark:/12148/cb16974300s.
sources.title: Rey, Georges (1908–2011) — BnF authority record
sources.creator: Bibliothèque nationale de France
sources.researchNote: The notice gives 27 May 1908 in Papeete, Tahiti, and 6 January 2011 in Bazas, Gironde. It describes Rey as a Tahitian composer, singer and musician and records Tihoti-Ré and Tihoti-Re as pseudonymous forms. Its cited sources include the Pathé disc of “O chant d’amour de Tahiti !” and Claude Lestrade’s 1992 article in the Journal de la Société des océanistes.

personNameVariants.publicNote: Tahitian pseudonym, given in the BnF person authority record as Tihoti-Ré or Tihoti-Re, with a see-also reference under that form. Tihoti is the Tahitian rendering of Georges. The Pathé disc credits the performing group as Tihoti-ré et son ensemble tahitien and names Tihoti in the vocal duo, so the composer credited as G. Rey and the singer credited as Tihoti are the same man.
